topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening situates the lecture within the cancer course and introduces its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable clonal evolution toward cancer within a permissive cellular environment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for environmental cancer causation against competing explanations based on chance and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, including the role of metabolism in determining their activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why mutational initiation may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of exposure determines carcinogenic effects and conclude by recapping the mechanisms leading to that specificity.

topics.label: Investigating and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity is obtained and why establishing it remains methodologically difficult.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing recaps the lecture's conclusions and frames their practical significance as everyday risk–benefit decisions.
